title: The other-checkout guard passes a cp whose target lands in the lane's own checkout
why: The other-checkout guard refused `cp "$B/$f" "$f"`, whose write landed in the lane's own checkout (lane lint-uses-pinned-tools, coordinator 01:03 CST Nov 8). A possible false alarm.
note: Triage read of the guard's record, decision an-agent-outside-its-home-tree-must-stop (00:59 CST Nov 8): its Ceiling says a target named through a variable the scan cannot resolve is not seen, so a plain `cp "$B/$f" "$f"` should pass; a refusal points to the cwd (a cwd in another checkout, or a `cd` earlier in the same command) rather than the cp. First step: get the exact command line, the cwd and the refusal text from the lane; red case first if the guard is wrong. Queue fix (owner 13:20 CST Nov 7). Related done step other-checkout-scratch-false-alarm. Slug from the coordinator. Filed 01:00 CST Nov 8. Exact case (lane, 01:02 CST Nov 8): cwd /home/user/claude-settings/.claude/worktrees/lane-merge-1417 (an EnterWorktree tree), no earlier cd. Command: `B=<primary>/.claude/worktrees/agent-a582f428fa2aafe42; for f in bin/ci-job ...; do cp "$B/$f" "$f"; done; grep ...`. Refusal: `PreToolUse:Bash hook error: other-checkout: Rule (other checkout): this write lands in another checkout ...`. The cp source is the other checkout (a read); the target `"$f"` is relative, in the cwd. So the guard resolved `$B` from the same-command assignment and read the cp source as the write target: a false alarm, ready for a lane. Red case first on this command; a control where a cp whose target is under `$B` still refuses. Second sighting (triage, 01:07 CST Nov 8): the guard also refused triage's own Bash call whose python heredoc only quoted this command as text, from the triage-roadmap worktree; the scan reads command words inside a heredoc body. Lane session_013NEJL3R2CBFavz7grtbJY8 started (coordinator, 01:06 CST Nov 8).
